text:
marta: quick heads-up — I started bringing up the new starlark-embed checkpoint in int6 hybrid on staging. initial synth recall@10 shows a drop for very short queries (<8 tokens). opening thread to collect quick triage.
jia: can you paste the numbers? short queries vs long?
omar: paste from the run earlier:
```
fp16 (baseline): recall@10 = 0.842
int6-hybrid: recall@10 = 0.776  # short queries (<8 tokens)
int6-hybrid (>=8 tokens): recall@10 = 0.835
delta_short = -6.6% abs
```
omar: note overall mean is only -0.3% but short-tail is the hit.
marta: thanks. did you run with or without L2 rescale? how about embedding norm drift?
jia: ran with per-channel quant + static clipping from calibration set. no extra post-rescale. distribution shift: median L2 norm down ~3.2% after quant.
lee: is this happening across all centroids or concentrated? any cluster collapse? tried silhouette quick check — a few anchor clusters moved.
nina: I looked at nearest-neigh counts: short queries get fewer top-1 matches (idflip up). k1 drops ~9% in that cohort.
omar: full notas from eval:
- dataset: short-query holdout (20k queries)
- metric: recall@10, recall@1, idflip
- fp16 vs int6-hybrid as above
- t-sne/umap shows local neighbors reordering, esp for code-like short queries
marta: hypothesis: quantization shrinks magnitude for short prompts due to activation range being tighter. can try per-layer scale refit or L2 rescale per vector post-quant.
jia: two quick experiments we can run today:
1) re-normalize embeddings after quant (divide by L2, multiply baseline mean norm)
2) per-channel symmetric quant with higher clip percentile (99.999 -> 99.9999)
omaR: (typo) omar: i'll kick both off as small A/Bs against the holdout.
ci-bot: test run queued — job id ci/emb-4391, runs: re-norm, clip+sym. i'll post results.
lee: also check tokenization edge-case: short queries often single-token code snippets, the model uses a different attention pattern. maybe prefix trimming changes KV shape impacting quant activation stats.
marta: agree. if re-norm recovers >3% absolute on recall@10 for short queries we can ship as interim fix. if not, consider fp16 fallback for short-query route in routing policy.
omar: quick ask — add logging for query token count in production trace (low sampling) so we can measure traffic distribution before deciding route.
jia: noted. i'll add a small sampling flag to trace and push the config.
ci-bot: job ci/emb-4391 completed. results summary:
- re-norm: recall@10 short = 0.812 (improvement, still -3.0% vs fp16)
- sym+clip tweak: recall@10 short = 0.828 (within -1.4% of fp16)
- resource note: sym+clip increases decode time ~1.8% on staging GPUs
marta: great. schedule follow-up: if sym+clip meets perf SLA and recall delta <1.5%, we can enable model variant with that quant profile and enable canary routing for short-query traffic.
lee: i'll open a PR with the quant profile and add canary config (traffic slice 1%).
nina: adding eval notebook (umap + idflip hist) to the ticket so SRE/product can review UX impact.
marta: thanks all. closing thread for now — next steps in ticket: #ENG-ML-9257. :white_check_mark:
